Priority Items 3.1 New ‘home’ for the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Graduate Programs update - Faculty have expressed concern that the details of this administrative move raise concerns about preferential treatment within colleges and administrators’ ability to replace program leaders at will with no input or involvement from faculty.
FSEC members noted that dean interference in curriculum would certainly rise to the level of senate involvement, but there may be no clear path for senate involvement in these personnel changes.
It was suggested that affected personnel contact their union and that the FSEC continue to monitor similar activity and be ready to respond to instances of encroachment into faculty rights. 3.2 Future Legislation Updates i.

Honors to update UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 to comport with the TAAC bill approved on 1/22 - Given that Honors as an Academic Experience has now been created in Kuali, some of the language in these sections can likely be pared down.
FS Pres.
Williams will remind the Honors Director that a formal bill will need to be presented to the Faculty Senate asap. ii.
Establishing College Liaisons - FSEC officers are still trying to convey to both deans and senators the myriad benefits of having a defined interface between the senate and the colleges.
A more structured information conduit would improve communications in both directions.
Currently, although senators are expected to take information back to their departments and bring concerns forward to the senate from them, the results on the ground are disparate and are generally found wanting in departments not currently represented in the senate.
The mechanics of adding a liaison to each college are still being debated and the goal is an equitable solution that honors the apportionment formula as stated in the By-Laws.

It was noted that the COE Dean has invited a brief ‘senate update’ at the next all-college meeting and it is hoped that other colleges may follow suit.
Such practice could help fill the communications gap until Liaisons can be ensconced in the Manual.
FSEC members agreed that the real 1

benefits of having liaisons may not emerge until 3 or 4 years after the roles are created, as it may take that long for representatives to realize the degree to which governance standards and norms across colleges are lacking and to develop remedies. iii.
Chapter 8 amendments related to 7- & 14-week calendar alignment - Staff will convert the administration’s draft to a formal bill and send it to CBUM for review.
It will be introduced at the 2/19 FS meeting but no vote will be held before March 12. iv. approval of academic calendars 8 years in advance - The ACC has drafted a proposal based on needs expressed by the Graduate School.

The draft will require review and support from CBUM and already has support from Online and Summer Programs. v. adjusting due date for final grades - discussed as part of Item 3.4 below. 3.3 Missing Classroom Database - Update - The Chairs of the CTI and JCSC are working to restore and update the data and will circle back with FSEC as needed. 3.4 Review Next Senate Agenda - 2/19/26 FS meeting - Several items were substantively discussed, especially the presentation of UM Chapter 2, the proposed amendments to previously approved FSEC Bills #4 and #5, the logistics of the VP election, and the addition of an initial discussion on adjusting the due date of final grades to accommodate calculation of academic standing, if time allows.

Add Senate approval of a new CHILD Institute ii.

Online calendars 2028-2031 3.5 Advance Planning - AY 26-27 FS meeting schedule (tabled until after the 2/19 VP election) 3.6 Connecting UDC with SCLC - FSEC’s concerns about the SCLC ‘subcommittees’ proposal have been conveyed to the Committee and liaison Van Wyk met with a committee representative recently.
Frustration about the UDC was expressed in that the SCLC would not have proposed new overlapping groups if it had confidence that their activities and initiatives might already be covered by the UDC.
Getting any information about the UDC’s current efforts has proven challenging.
If communication is a key stumbling block, FSEC felt that a joint meeting of some sort would help break the impasse.
A meeting of full committees might prove unwieldy right away so it was agreed that a 6-person event might be an option as an opening effort.
It would involve the UDC Co-Chairs, the SCLC Chair and liaison, and the FS Pres. and VP.
The SCLC would like to propose that their committee have a representative or liaison to the UDC to help ensure consistent communications.

The FS Pres. will address some of these concerns in his next meeting with University leadership. 3.7 Staffing IPC and SAC - The IPC has been staffed and the Coordinator has corrected a communication error related to updating the membership.

Staff will get up to date information and work with the FS President to fill all seats. 3.8 Grade dispute procedures (8.26.13) and academic dishonesty procedures (8.27.17) 4.

of the library were represented in the search.

Invited Guest: Amy D’Agata, CRCA Chair at 1:00 PM - Chair D’Agata reminded FSEC of the scope of her committee and noted the responsibilities are both varied and numerous.
She explained that even with recent UM updates that refined the committee’s priorities and added members, the committee still struggles to give every issue under their purview its due.
FSEC indicated a willingness to consider structural changes if they would improve efficiency and ensure a manageable workload.
Chair D’Agata noted she views their most important responsibility to be that of providing advice to the VP RED regarding research-related activities.
It has been an especially challenging year in that regard due to dramatic shifts in the research funding landscape.
Considering the very close relationship of the Committee with the VP RED’s office, it was suggested that it should perhaps be a Joint rather than a Senate Committee to help ensure adequate expertise and staffing levels to accomplish priority tasks.

If this is not workable, it was suggested that perhaps the Competitive Grants Subcommittee, at a minimum, could move in that direction since that group is so reliant on administrative help from the Research Office and on volunteer reviewers that are not part of the senate.
Such configuration might also help ensure expertise is brought to bear from across research-centric academic units.
Sen.
Meenach, liaison to the CRCA, noted that the grants activity is a huge service burden and it requires the participation of expert reviewers.
She concurred that the best structure would be to make it a Joint Committee under the VPRED with senate representation provided for alongside other faculty members and administrators.
The group moved on to discuss the F&A oversight (Facilities and Administration, also known as ‘overhead’) responsibilities of the Committee.
Chair D’Agata and Sen.
Meenach noted that with the budget model transition, which involves a new and somewhat opaque subvention formula and which has increased Dean discretion, the Committee’s ability to influence decision-making has become constrained.

Committee members have inquired if the level of effort involved in the review and assessment is really worth it.
FSEC agreed that the CRCA Chair and her committee, along with the FSEC liaison, should develop a formal proposal to restructure their committee.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-12 Introduction: April 10, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting For Approval: May 1, 2025 Proposed Revisions to Appendix C of the University Manual By-Laws of the Faculty Senate Amendments pertain to converting the Special Budget and Administration Committee to a Permanent Standing Committee (According to Section 12.1 of the By-Laws, amendments require two meetings and a two-thirds majority vote of senators present to pass.) RATIONALE: According to Article II, Section 4 of Appendix B of the University Manual (Constitution of the Faculty Senate), the Senate shall establish such standing and special committees as it deems necessary to carry out its functions.
During AY 2023-2024, the University community faced operational changes, including various administrative policy initiatives and the planned transition to a new budget model, then known as IBB.
The proposed pace of change and the sheer quantity of new initiatives strained the ability of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) to respond appropriately and react in a coordinated, meaningful, and timely fashion.

The FSEC concluded that creating a special committee to advise them in these and related matters would improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Faculty Senate.
A new group, known as the Special Budget and Administration Committee (SBAC) was created in May 2024 and was designed to exist through AY 2025-2026.
The charge of the committee was generally to advise the Senate on administrative policy developments, assist in analyzing and making recommendations regarding any major operational changes emerging under the university strategic plan, and analyze the effects of the new budget model and its implementation, as well as any other specific operational expenditures relevant to faculty.
The current FSEC has found the Special Committee to be useful and effective and has noted that other faculty senates at peer institutions have permanent committees focused on budgetary matters.
The FSEC therefore recommends that the special committee now become a permanent standing committee.

MOTION: THAT THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE BE INSERTED INTO APPENDIX C 4.90 The Budget and Administration Committee (BAC) shall comprise five faculty members, three of whom shall be faculty senators.
The chair shall serve a two-year term and will be elected by the committee following input from the faculty senate executive committee.
The Committee shall provide reports on their activities to the Faculty Senate at least annually and more often as directed by the FSEC or the Senate.

Any specific BAC proposals for action will flow from the Committee to the FSEC and then to the Senate. 4.91 Activities of the Budget and Administration Committee will include but not be limited to: the review and, if necessary, the development of measures for tracking major or incremental expenditures, with the aim of ensuring balanced support of faculty interests; requesting information on the university’s performance toward any new goals set up under the prevailing budget model and under any proposed changes to the budget model, and raising questions about the correspondence of these allocations against performance metrics (KPIs) and the university’s Strategic Plan; monitoring administrative policies with the aim of supporting academic freedom and faculty efforts.
The Committee shall make recommendations to the executive committee and the senate about formal responses to: any plans or proposals by the committees and individuals tasked with the implementation and functioning of the budget model; any positions or policy initiatives of the institutional research office, administrative policy groups, purchasing, capital projects, and similar groups as they may identify or that arise.

They may also engage in advocacy on behalf of the faculty for support of research, instruction, professional development, travel, course caps, and service time, so that faculty thrive in their work given their contractual roles.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-3 January 23, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting Context (from JCODL 2022-2023 final report): “Several years ago (circa 2013), URI adopted definitions of online and blended learning (Face to face [< 25% online], Blended [25-75% online], and Online [75-100% online]), with the implicit, but unstated, assumption that the online portion was asynchronous.
The COVID era of remote instruction gave rise to additional approaches to remote instruction and the need to reflect all available modality options and to provide clear, comprehensible and accessible definitions and descriptions for the benefit of faculty and students.” Rationale: Definitions for Course Methods of Instruction are not currently memorialized in the University Manual and the current need to update related descriptions provides an opportunity to ensconce standardized language in the University Manual, where it will be easily found and understood.
The language is proposed for insertion into Chapter 8, Academic Regulations (Regulations for Students), Section 30, Courses.

Making JCODL’s suggested changes requires removing ‘Online’ from the approved ‘Methods of Instruction’ and removing the term “in class” from the descriptions of ‘Laboratory’ and ‘Studio’.
Because over 770 current ‘online’-method courses will need to be assigned to one of the other methods, faculty/departments will be allowed to update the method of current ‘online’ courses directly with the registrar without going through the standard course modification process.
Due to the volume of required changes, the new methods will take effect starting in the Fall 2026 semester.
